newsitem.title: UK: Brazil tells ACPC its coffee exports exceed quotas.
newsitem.headline: Brazil tells ACPC its coffee exports exceed quotas.

text.p: Brazil has told the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) that it was likely to exceed the 15-million bag export quota for the one-year period ending June 30, 1997 by 1.2 million bags or eight percent, the ACPC said.
The notification, received by the London-based ACPC last week, has been circulated to the other member states of the 14-member grouping.
ACPC secretary-general Robeiro Oliveira Silva said on Monday so far there had been no response from fellow producer members.
"The chairman of the ACPC has received a notification from the Brazilian government stating that it is likely to overshoot the export target of 15 million (bags) by eight percent," Silva said.
The ACPC is chaired by Rubens Barbosa, the Brazilian ambassador to the UK.
Under the current ACPC export programme expiring at the end of the month, the Brazilian exports are kept at nine million bags from July to December 1996 and six million from January to June 1997.
The group agreed at a meeting last month to extend the export programme by 12 more months from July.

The members' exports will be capped at 52.75 million bags and about the same as the volume limit set under the expiring scheme. But individual quotas will not be set until the next meeting in September.
